aoi.name: กรุงเทพมหานคร
aoi.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap relation R92277 via Nominatim lookup
aoi.rationale: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration, the full administrative extent the project plan names as the post-pilot target. Admin level 4, not a hand-drawn box, so population, network and reporting geographies all refer to the same place.

osm_extract.content_sha256: to be recorded per run from the staged file
osm_extract.rationale: A single regional extract replaces tiled Overpass queries. Overpass is the right tool for one district and the wrong tool for 1,643 km2; the extract is read locally with GDAL's OSM driver, so no osmium dependency and no API rate limiting.

analysis_crs_decision.justification: Unchanged from the pilot. UTM zone 47N covers the whole BMA at a point scale factor within 0.1 percent, so one projected CRS serves both the pilot district and the city without re-projection artefacts at the seam.
analysis_crs_decision.note: Bangkok is far larger than the pilot, so the scale factor varies more across the city than across the district. Lengths and areas remain metric and usable for screening.

aggregation_grid.note: Public aggregation is fixed at 1 km across the city. At 1,643 km2 the 100 m mesh produces tens of millions of rows with no analytical benefit and a real disclosure risk in sparse outer districts.

scale_limits.routing: Destination-centric Dijkstra over a compressed routing index, not per-person A*
scale_limits.flood: NOT DERIVED at city scale in this build. See docs/CITY_SCALE_LIMITATIONS.md.
scale_limits.reason: The only reachable open terrain source has a vertical error of roughly 5-10 m in Bangkok, which is larger than the entire flood-relevant elevation range of 0-2 m. A stage-based depth surface derived from it would be noise.

notes: The Khlong San pilot remains the reference case for anything requiring flood depth or evacuation.
City artefacts and pilot artefacts are separate runs; a city run never silently substitutes for a pilot result.
